article_limitations: Disposition aggregate_only: the source reports a prospective case series of 140 patients (158 knees) with knee osteoarthritis treated with ACP only through group-level means, confidence intervals, counts, percentages and regression coefficients; no patient has individual identity evidence or an individually described course, so no individual patient records are created and group statements are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 140 (literal) and roster_complete is false because none of the 140 stated individuals can be enumerated.

Table 1 prints the baseline NRS-pain row as "62 (1.9)" while the abstract, Table 2 and the results text give a baseline mean NRS-pain of 6.2 on a 0 to 10 scale (Table 2: 6.2 (5.8–6.5)); the missing decimal point is treated as a print artefact (ambiguity, not a source conflict) and is not corrected.

The Table 1 row "Bilateral treatment, n" is printed truncated as "18 (" with no closing value; the discussion states that 18 patients with bilateral complaints were included. The Table 1 header counts N = 158 (knees) while rows such as age and female sex are described per patient ("Baseline characteristics of 140 included patients (158 knees)"); whether each row uses patients or knees as its denominator is not stated by the source.

All patients received 3 ACP injections; 43 patients received 1 of the 3 injections with a 2-week interval and all others had a 1-week interval. The source does not identify which patients these were, so the schedule is not attributable to individuals.

The statement that the group lost to follow-up at 12 months "consisted of more men (64%)" is a subgroup statement with no printed group size or denominator; it is not attributed to individual patients.

Figure 1 (recruitment flowchart) prints "Patients included in analysis (n = 140)" with sub-items of 123 patients with one-sided treatment and 18 with bilateral treatment, which add to 141; 140 patients with 18 bilateral treatments matches the 158 knees printed in the same box and in the text. These counts are pixel content recorded only in the visual target; the mismatch is not reconciled by the source.

Figures 1 to 3 are group-level figures (recruitment flowchart and two mean-score plots); ownership is aggregate. Pixels were reviewed in the separate visual target; no values were read from plot geometry. Values printed inside the images are recorded only in that visual target.
